feedback: Pre-race review, based only on earlier races and the candidate's contents. Nothing has raced for this candidate, so this states no outcome for it. The candidate is valid: five sensor positions with outer x at +/-0.07 and inner at +/-0.03 and 0 (y = 0.03), five weights matching them, and kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction are all inside their ranges. It matches iteration 10 (score 56.8458, the best raced design) field for field, so it is the best-measured design available. Iteration 10 improved on iteration 8 mainly through slalom progress (0.036 to 0.111), with s-bend flat at 0.0415. Its oval line_loss_events rose from 1.7 to 2.2 and oval steering_oscillation was 0.16, so the oval is the weak spot. Those oval numbers were measured on development tracks, not the unseen track. Every run on every track still ended off_track, with max_error about 0.060 to 0.063 m. Testing base_speed 1.6 now would be an untested step on the final, once-scored race, and iteration 9 showed that a one-field change can cost points. Approve it unchanged. After the race, the telemetry is for the record only, since there is no later iteration to act on it. Watch whether the unseen track's line losses and off-track exits look like the oval's pattern.
requested_changes: No change for this race: approve iteration 10's design (kd 0.3, base_speed 1.5, kp 2.5, ki 0.5, outer sensors +/-0.07) unchanged, because it is the best raced design at 56.8458 and any single-field step is untested.

If a later review of this design were possible, the first candidate change would be controller.base_speed 1.6 with all other fields fixed, citing iteration 8's oval progress gain from 1.4 to 1.5 (0.2261 to 0.2657), but only if oval line_loss_events stays at or below 2.2 and noise_robustness does not drop.
